subject: Seat-slicing proposal and feature-bundle tradeoffs for MedSync

From: Alex Chen <alex@medsync.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-24T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging question — seat granularity and add-on bundling

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. The team liked the low latency on conversational reranking, but we have an internal wrinkle on packaging I hoped you could help with.

Our usage pattern is spiky: clinicians run heavy batches overnight and smaller chats during the day. We want to avoid paying for idle dedicated seats yet guarantee throughput for overnight jobs. Two questions:

1) Can Redwood support "seat-slicing" — i.e., splitting a single Dedicated seat into fractional concurrency units that can be reserved for high-throughput windows?

2) How do feature bundles apply to this model? Specifically, we only need advanced observability and can skip the Optimize add-on initially. Can we purchase core inference capacity and attach observability as a per-seat add-on?

We'd appreciate an example proposal and rough pricing bands to take to procurement.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of AI, MedSync Health

--
MedSync Health | alex@medsync.ai
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@medsync.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-24T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — seat granularity and add-on bundling

Alex — thanks for the clear summary, glad the demo landed. Short answers up front: yes on fractional seat reservations (we call it seat-slicing internally) and yes on attaching observability as a per-seat add-on.

I'm attaching a brief proposal (Seat_Slicing_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a pricing workbook (FeatureBundle_Pricing_Tiers.xlsx) for two sample configurations:
- Night-burst pooling: 4 full seats reserved, plus 8 fractional slices purchasable in 0.25 increments for burst windows.
- Daylight elastic: smaller baseline reserved capacity (1–2 full seats) with slices to scale to expected daytime concurrency.

Key tradeoffs to call out:
- Seat-slicing reduces committed spend but increases scheduling complexity. If your overnight jobs are highly parallel, reserved full seats reduce head-of-line latency for large batches.
- Observability as an add-on is priced per seat-slice; full-seat entitlements get a small discount.

Can Karthik and Marcus confirm the latency SLO implications for fractional slices vs full seats? I'll plan to follow up with a pricing band you can present to procurement.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Tessa / Marcus — quick tech note for the thread:

- Fractional slices are implemented as time-sliced reservations on the dedicated pool with soft affinity. For short, high-throughput batches ( > 2k tokens/request and > 50 concurrent requests), you will notice ~5–15ms additional scheduling jitter compared to a fully pinned seat; steady-state token latency is unaffected.
- For jobs that rely on very large KV caches, recommend reserving at least one full seat per worker to host warm caches — slices share KV cache capacity and warm-up can add 10–30s for the first large batch.

If MedSync can tolerate the jitter window above for their overnight runs, seat-slicing will materially reduce their committed spend.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

If you can put both items in a single slide or short PDF, we'll circulate internally.

Best,
Alex

Alex / Procurement — attached is a short slide PDF (Seat_Slicing_Proposal_v1.pdf) and an export from our pricing workbook summarizing:

- 12-month committed: 4 reserved full seats + 8 slices (0.25 increments) + observability on full seats = $128,000/year (approx) — includes 10% volume discount and one onboarding credit equivalent to $8k (one-off).
- 3-month seasonal: same configuration priced pro-rata at $38,000/quarter — no onboarding credit; observability priced at a 12% premium per-slice.

We can offer a middle ground: 6-months commit with a $4k onboarding credit and a 5% unit discount. If you want to formalize that, I'll get legal to generate a short amendment and route to DocuSign.

Next steps: if Procurement is comfortable, flag which contract term (12|6|3 months) and we'll prepare a term sheet. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the slide.
